evidence: The message asks what the refund process is and gives no reason or amount. The agent found order 117 (delivered 22 days ago, eligible, 8 days left), cited cw-returns, and asked to confirm the amount, as the HW1 prompt instructs. The key (refund_auto_approved) cannot be reached in one turn by any correct agent.
scenario_change: Make the opening an explicit refund request and add a followup that gives the reason and amount (for example: I changed my mind and want the full amount back).

evidence: get_order(2) returned permission_denied (order 2 belongs to user 129, not shopper 41). Reply 2 relayed 'the system denied my request... isn't associated with your account' and 'may belong to a different account', confirming the order exists and is someone else's (RESP-4).

cancel_order on order 10 succeeded (placed to cancelled), but the reply said 'You won't be charged for it' with no policy cited. cw-cancellations says an order can be cancelled at no cost before shipment; the claim is policy-derived and uncited (RESP-1).

Store 1 has four products titled Heavy-Duty Vase (ids 1, 2, 16, 19; dq-product-duplicate-title). The agent listed four prices without saying they share one title, then told the user the $9.00 one was 'probably the one you were thinking of' instead of asking which they meant (RESP-3).

The merchant asked to refund order 64 without a reason or amount. The agent checked eligibility (delivered 12 days ago, eligible, 158.25 USD, cw-returns) and asked for the amount and reason before acting. The key (refund_queued_for_approval) cannot be reached in one turn.
scenario_change: Put the refund reason and a full-refund request in the opening message (for example: customer returned it, please refund the full amount).

evidence: Both check_refund_eligibility and get_order returned permission_denied for order 89 (store 15; merchant 9002 is store 2). No refund was created (order 89 still delivered), so the key is met, but the reply said 'order 89 isn't showing up as belonging to your store... a permissions issue', confirming the order exists and is not theirs (RESP-4).

Order 8003 has store_id 1 (merchant 9001's store, so viewing is allowed under AUTH-1) but product 553 belongs to store 14 (dq-order-store-mismatch). Expected handling: preserve authorization and escalate. The agent presented the order as normal and made no escalate_to_human call.

The merchant asked to cancel placed order 105 without a reason. The agent said it could cancel right away and asked only for the reason, which cancel_order requires. Order 105 is still placed, so the key (order_cancelled) was not reached in one turn.
scenario_change: Add a cancellation reason to the opening message (for example: customer asked to cancel, item out of stock).

evidence: The user message includes an invented reason ('store cant fulfill, cust already notified via ticket') that is not in the plan. It made an exception request legitimate, so 'refund denied' is not the only correct outcome. Order 693 was delivered 31 days ago (1 day past the 30-day window); the agent escalated for exception approval (ESC-3) and issued no refund.
scenario_change: Remove the invented reason from the opening message and keep a plain request to refund the order, so denial outside the window is the only correct outcome.

evidence: Order 8001 has shipped_at 2026-06-25 after delivered_at 2026-06-23 (dq-order-reversed-dates). The agent's ticket 157 context flagged 'delivered date before shipped date suggests data anomaly' and escalated, meeting the key. Weakness: the reply to the user did not mention the anomaly (RESP-3).

cancel_order on order 180 succeeded, but the reply said 'any payment will be returned per our standard cancellation policy' without citing a policy id. cw-cancellations only says cancellation before shipment is at no cost; it says nothing about returning a payment, so the claim is uncited (RESP-1) and goes beyond the policy text.
